title: Free Gemini “Tasks” Now Available in Six Countries – 9to5Google Announces Global Rollout
body:
Google has opened the door to a broader audience for its Gemini “tasks” feature, formerly known as Spark, by making it free for users in six countries. Until now, the capability—designed to let users break down complex prompts into step‑by‑step instructions—was locked behind the AI Pro subscription tier. The change, rolled out today, signals Google’s intent to accelerate adoption of its generative‑AI tools and to compete more aggressively with rival offerings from OpenAI and Microsoft.

The tasks function, introduced as part of the Gemini suite of AI models, allows users to submit a single request that the system then splits into a series of sub‑tasks, each executed in sequence to produce a refined result. For example, a user could ask Gemini to “plan a weekend trip to Kyoto, book flights, and create a daily itinerary,” and the model would handle each component automatically. Previously, this advanced workflow required a paid AI Pro plan, limiting its reach to power users and early adopters. By extending free access to residents of the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Australia, Germany, and Japan, Google hopes to showcase the practical value of Gemini in everyday productivity scenarios.

Industry analysts view the move as a strategic response to the rapid expansion of AI‑driven productivity tools. OpenAI’s ChatGPT Plus and Microsoft’s Copilot have already been bundled into premium subscriptions, prompting concerns that high‑cost barriers could slow user engagement. Google’s decision to democratize a key feature may help it capture a larger share of the burgeoning market for AI assistants that go beyond simple chat. “Free access to tasks lowers the friction for casual users to experience what generative AI can actually do for them,” says Priya Desai, a senior analyst at TechInsights. “It’s a classic ‘freemium’ tactic that can convert a sizable portion of users into paid subscribers once they see the value.”

The rollout also reflects Google’s broader push to integrate Gemini more tightly across its ecosystem. The company has been embedding the model into Search, Workspace, and Android, positioning it as the backbone of its next‑generation AI experience. By allowing free users to experiment with multi‑step workflows, Google gathers valuable data on how people interact with the technology, informing future refinements and helping the model learn from real‑world use cases. Moreover, the six countries selected for the initial launch represent markets where Google already enjoys strong brand recognition and high mobile penetration, providing a fertile testing ground before a wider global release.

Critics, however, caution that the free offering could raise privacy and data‑security questions. Gemini’s tasks involve processing potentially sensitive information—travel plans, personal schedules, and financial details—through multiple AI stages. Google has reiterated that data is anonymized and used to improve model performance, but regulators in Europe and elsewhere continue to scrutinize how large tech firms handle user data in AI contexts. Consumer‑rights groups urge transparent disclosures and robust opt‑out mechanisms to ensure that the convenience of automated tasks does not come at the expense of privacy.

Looking ahead, the free availability of Gemini tasks may set a new benchmark for AI service pricing across the tech industry. If user adoption spikes, Google could leverage the feature to upsell other premium services, such as higher‑resolution image generation or real‑time translation. The company’s next steps are likely to involve expanding the free rollout beyond the initial six nations and adding deeper integration with third‑party apps via APIs. As generative AI becomes an increasingly central part of digital workflows, the ability to automate complex, multi‑step processes without a subscription fee could reshape how individuals and businesses approach everyday problem‑solving, positioning Gemini as a pivotal tool in the evolving AI landscape.
